title: Siapo painted bark cloth
summary: Samoan siapo is bark cloth painted by hand with a fibre brush in brown dye: flowers, leaves and vines are laid freely across the pale cloth. Copy the design, which mirrors both ways.
howToPlay: Pick a dye and a painted shape.
Paint it; the mirrored copies are painted too.
Check the cloth against the design.
Watch and learn shows a finished round, one placement at a time.
rules: The cloth mirrors left to right and top to bottom.
Placing the same shape in the same colour again, or choosing the eraser, clears it and its mirror partners.
The result compares your piece with the pattern cell by cell: three stars at 98 percent or more, two at 85, one at 60.
The pattern to copy is always shown beside the work and as a faint guide on the cloth.
heritageNote: Siapo is the painted bark cloth of Samoa, beaten from mulberry bark and decorated by hand with fibre brushes and brown dyes. Makers share designs of flowers, leaves and vines across generations.
credits: Pattern designs are original arrangements in the tradition's motif vocabulary.
